First practise the figueta (thumb and index finger), then the dedilho (index finger striking up and down), and then the trinado (a triplet ornament), glissando, single-string plucking and tremolo. Accompanying in the Lisbon style, play an introduction built on the second half of the melody and then answer the singer with short phrases; in the Coimbra style, a downstroke of the thumb rolls across all the strings with the index finger crossed in front of it, in harmony with the acoustic guitar.

The Portuguese guitar (guitarra portuguesa) is a plucked instrument of Portugal in Europe, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322-5. It has twelve steel strings in six double courses, and is played with the corner of the fingernail, the traditional fingerings including the figueta, which uses only thumb and index finger, and the dedilho, which strikes up and down with the index finger. It is common in fado accompaniment and as a solo instrument, and it also appears in concert halls and at classical and world music festivals; the Coimbra style is associated with the nocturnal serenades of university students.
